submission.name: Lookahead rounds, everything computed again
submission.description: Built for the reaction-depth track, from Lookahead rounds, states measured away. Forward rounds clear nothing: the registers a round is done with are measured away in the X basis, and the round that undoes it, which forms those values anyway, corrects their phase. That more than halves the operations of a forward round, and the circuit spends them on computing more often and holding less: to undo a compression, the output of the one before is computed again from the search register, with nothing else held. A value computed again is no deeper than the first time, so this costs no depth. The most the circuit holds is what the header's second block needs by itself, with its schedule in place over the nonce. A round keeps one register beyond the state, not two. 1,130 qubits at reaction depth 4,331, against 1,249 at 4,435.

submission.name: Recomputed schedule
submission.description: The oracle on 914 qubits. As in the 1,072-qubit entry, each intermediate hash is measured away and its phase removed later. The header's second block, which set that count, no longer holds 16 schedule words: only two of its message words are quantum, so it holds seven words in progress and computes the older ones again from those two when a step needs them, in two spare registers. Its uncomputation subtracts and measures away the kept state first, which leaves room for an ordinary schedule. Four times the baseline's Toffolis.

submission.name: Kept carries, 16,384 qubits
submission.description: Kept carries built on 16,384 qubits instead of 65,536. An addition whose carries are left in qubits of their own is undone by CNOTs and measurements, with no Toffoli, so each spare qubit saves one Toffoli of the backward pass. With 16,384 qubits, 13,217 of the 101,985 ANDs of the forward pass are kept and the rest are computed twice. The forward pass is the same: classical inputs stay classical, and the last compression computes only the three compared words. 189,744 Toffolis per shot, against 140,592 on 65,536 qubits and the baseline's 262,158 on 2,000.

submission.name: Measured-away states, 1,074 qubits
submission.description: The 1,072-qubit oracle with two more qubits. Intermediate hashes are measured away and their phases removed later, so the circuit holds one compression at a time. In the 34 rounds of the header's second block that have no scratch, the two extra qubits carry Gidney's constant adder: carries are measured as they are used, and the phases are removed by XORing the carries twice into borrowed busy qubits. A round constant there costs 89 Toffolis at most instead of 558 on average.

submission.name: Baseline
submission.description: Plain reference construction: the five compressions built like the SHA-256 compression baseline, each with its own state register and all sharing one block register; classical inputs copied into qubits; the hash masked and compared to the target; then everything run backwards.

submission.name: Classical inputs kept classical
submission.description: Kept carries with no spare qubit: 3,167 qubits, the fewest that design can use. No AND is kept, so the backward pass computes each one again, and what is left is a forward pass of 101,985 ANDs. Only the 80 searched bits are qubits: sums of classical words are worked out on classical bits and enter as one addend, Ch and Maj with classical arguments need no AND, and nine rounds of the header's first block see no qubit. The last compression computes only the three compared words. No register is rewound between compressions, which is why it uses more qubits than the baseline. 202,961 Toffolis per shot, against the baseline's 262,158 on 2,000 qubits.

submission.name: Measured-away states
submission.description: The oracle on 1,072 qubits. Each intermediate hash is measured away in the X basis as soon as the next one exists, and the phase that leaves is removed later by computing the value again, so the circuit holds one compression and its inputs at a time. The header's second block sets the count: 48 idle extranonce qubits, the kept starting state, the working state and the 16-word schedule. Its last 34 rounds have no free qubit and use additions that keep their carries in the operand; everything else uses the baseline's arithmetic.

submission.name: Lookahead rounds, states measured away
submission.description: Built for the reaction-depth track. The five compressions use the rounds of Lean lookahead rounds (log-depth adders, new state words in fresh registers, dropped registers cleared by subtraction), which cost 7 reactions per round forward and 7 backward. A chaining value that is no longer needed is measured away in the X basis and its phase is corrected with Z gates when the value is computed again; a value computed again is no deeper than the first time, so this costs operations and no depth, and the circuit never holds more than two chaining values next to the compression it is working on. To fit twelve passes of 64 rounds into 20,000,000 operations, the adder keeps its propagate products in qubits and every carry-save row is written once. 1,249 qubits at reaction depth 4,435, against the baseline's 2,000 at 108,224.

submission.name: Kept carries, 32,768 qubits
submission.description: Kept carries built on 32,768 qubits instead of 65,536. An addition whose carries are left in qubits of their own is undone by CNOTs and measurements, with no Toffoli, so each spare qubit saves one Toffoli of the backward pass. With 32,768 qubits, 29,601 of the 101,985 ANDs of the forward pass are kept and the rest are computed twice. The forward pass is the same: classical inputs stay classical, and the last compression computes only the three compared words. 173,360 Toffolis per shot, against 140,592 on 65,536 qubits and the baseline's 262,158 on 2,000.

submission.name: Kept carries
submission.description: Built for the fewest Toffolis, on every qubit the problem allows. An addition whose carries are left in qubits of their own is undone by CNOTs and measurements, with no Toffoli, so each spare qubit saves one Toffoli of the backward pass. 62,369 of the 101,985 ANDs of the forward pass are kept this way and the rest are computed twice. Classical inputs stay classical: their sums are worked out on classical bits and enter as one addend, Ch and Maj with classical arguments need no AND, and nine rounds of the header's first block see no qubit. The last compression computes only the three compared words, and skips the rounds an easy exponent does not need. 65,536 qubits and 140,592 Toffolis per shot, against the baseline's 2,000 and 262,158.

submission.name: Trimmed constants and tail
submission.description: The baseline architecture with hand-written adders. Each round constant is reduced by a few units to gain trailing zeros, which a constant adder skips, and free carry-ins on the neighbouring additions make up the difference. Two additions in a row into one register share their lowest bit, saving a Toffoli. The last two schedule words are never stored: their terms are added straight into the state. Saves 649 Toffolis and 2 qubits over the folded first rounds.

submission.name: Lean lookahead rounds, 818 qubits
submission.description: The rounds of Lean lookahead rounds, with new state words in fresh registers and dropped ones subtracted away, and an adder that takes the word in four parts of eight bits in place of two halves. That adder needs 18 scratch qubits, not 26, and is deeper: 818 qubits at reaction depth 667. It sits on the reaction-depth front just below Lean lookahead rounds.

submission.name: qSHA256, Toffoli-only
submission.description: Reconstruction of the garbage-free SHA-256 circuit of the qSHA256 project in its default architecture (Cuccaro adder, rolling schedule, serial rounds, full uncomputation). X, CNOT and Toffoli only, no measurement. Rebuilt by sha256.fail from the project's source at commit 741fe86; the project's own code was not run.

submission.name: Balanced lookahead rounds, Brent-Kung
submission.description: The circuit of Balanced lookahead rounds with Brent-Kung carry trees for the sums of a round as well, in place of Sklansky trees. A Brent-Kung tree has fewer nodes, so this variant needs fewer qubits and Toffolis, and it is deeper: 1,060 qubits, 77,304 Toffolis, reaction depth 905. Every AND is computed once into a qubit of its own and measured away, and registers are cleared by an X-basis measurement with the phase fixed on the bits of a second sum.

submission.name: Balanced lookahead rounds, compact
submission.description: Balanced lookahead rounds with its scratch cut down, still below 1,000 in reaction depth and below 100,000 Toffolis: 916 qubits, 97,249 Toffolis, reaction depth 905. The carries of a sum that forms a register are built in place and become the register. A dropped register is measured before the sum that fixes its phase is computed, so its qubits are free during it. Sums that only fix a phase merge some carries in place with a Toffoli, trading Toffolis for qubits. The two rows shared by a round's sums are held as one register and one carry row, and the ANDs they were made from are measured away while the rows are in use. Carry trees are Brent-Kung networks, except for a Sklansky network in the clearing step of the rewind.

submission.name: Carry-lookahead rounds
submission.description: Built for the reaction-depth track, where Toffolis are free. Every addition is a log-depth carry-lookahead adder (Sklansky prefix, carries erased with Draper's identity), and each round computes e' and a' into fresh registers as one carry-save sum, storing only carry rows: XOR-linear and degree-2 terms (Sigma, Ch, Maj) are built on the fly in reused helper qubits. The dropped registers d and h are measured in the X basis and their phase is fixed on a recomputation, so no state register is ever added into in place and phase-correction chains do not grow from round to round. 1,006 qubits at reaction depth 629, against 829 at 3,892 for the previous best.

submission.name: Folded first rounds
submission.description: The baseline with constant folding in rounds 0 to 3. The initial hash value is fixed, so round 0 reduces to two additions, round 1 needs no ANDs for Ch and Maj, and the round constants of rounds 1 to 3 are added at build time. Saves 372 Toffolis and no qubits.

submission.name: qSHA256, measurement-based
submission.description: Reconstruction of the garbage-free SHA-256 circuit of the qSHA256 project in its lowest-cost configuration: every Toffoli is a temporary AND, computed once and removed by measurement (Gidney adder, rolling schedule, serial rounds, full uncomputation). Rebuilt by sha256.fail from the project's source at commit 741fe86; the project's own code was not run.

submission.name: Balanced lookahead rounds, Sklansky
submission.description: The circuit of Balanced lookahead rounds with Sklansky carry trees for every sum of the rounds, the schedule and its rewind, in place of Brent-Kung trees where depth mattered less. It is a little shallower and uses more Toffolis: 1,113 qubits, 98,202 Toffolis, reaction depth 717. Every AND is computed once into a qubit of its own and measured away, and registers are cleared by an X-basis measurement with the phase fixed on the bits of a second sum.

submission.name: In-place rounds, 775 qubits
submission.description: Rounds in place on the eight state registers, seven additions a round, with a ripple adder whose carries are pebbled: the carry into a bit is made from an earlier carry whenever it is needed and unmade the same way, so an addition holds at most five carries at once. 775 qubits, seven more than the block and digest, at reaction depth 2,074. It sits on the reaction-depth front between Zero scratch and the other in-place entries. Built on the generator of Lean lookahead rounds.

submission.name: In-place rounds, 786 qubits
submission.description: Rounds in place on the eight state registers, with T1 added straight into d as two rows that are never stored, and an adder that takes the word in parts of eight bits and keeps the carry into each part. 786 qubits at reaction depth 926. K sits in the register of W during the round. It sits on the reaction-depth front between Zero scratch and Lean lookahead rounds. Built on the generator of Lean lookahead rounds.

submission.name: Compute, copy, uncompute
submission.description: The baseline built the textbook way: the state is computed in 256 scratch qubits, copied into the digest register, and uncomputed. Does not rely on the digest register starting at zero.

submission.name: Lean lookahead rounds
submission.description: Built for the reaction-depth track on the ideas of Carry-lookahead rounds, with most of its scratch and waiting removed. No carry-save row is stored: a bit of such a row is built in helper qubits for the gate that needs it, also when rows are nested. The registers a round drops are cleared by subtracting a recomputation in place, not measured, which needs no extra register and one reaction less. The adder's prefix network is aligned so that no carry is merged more than four times (AND-depth 5, and 5 reactions per step of the schedule rewind, not 6), and it works on the word in two parts with one carry kept between them, so it needs 26 scratch qubits, not 46. The last two schedule words are never formed. 826 qubits at reaction depth 581, against 1,006 at 629.

submission.name: In-place rounds, 782 qubits
submission.description: Rounds in place on the eight state registers, five additions a round, with an adder that takes the word in parts of four bits and keeps the carry into each part. 782 qubits at reaction depth 1,227. K + W + Sigma1 + Ch is reduced to two rows that are never stored and added into h as two additions. It sits on the reaction-depth front between Zero scratch and Lean lookahead rounds. Built on the generator of Lean lookahead rounds.

submission.name: Low-qubit adder
submission.description: The baseline with its adder replaced by the Cuccaro ripple-carry adder, which needs one extra qubit instead of 31 carries and two Toffolis per bit instead of one.

submission.name: Baseline
submission.description: Plain reference construction: state computed in place in the digest register, message schedule expanded in place and rewound, measurement-based ripple-carry adders, one 32-qubit temporary.

submission.name: Balanced lookahead rounds
submission.description: Short on both counts at once: reaction depth 728 and 84,150 Toffolis, on 1,113 qubits. Every AND is computed once into a qubit of its own and measured away, which costs no Toffoli and only as many reactions as the tree of ANDs is deep; everything in between is an XOR of register qubits and those AND qubits. Each round forms e' and a' in fresh registers with one carry-save sum and one log-depth carry tree each, and the registers it drops are measured in the X basis with the phase fixed directly on the bits of a second sum. The schedule moves the same way, forwards and back. Carry trees are Sklansky networks where depth matters and Brent-Kung networks elsewhere.

submission.name: Zero scratch
submission.description: SHA-256 compression on exactly the 768 qubits of the block and digest registers, with no scratch qubit and no measurement: X, CNOT and Toffoli gates only. Additions keep their carries in the wires of the number being added. Sigma operands are made in place by CNOTs, and Ch and Maj are computed onto one of their own inputs. A round constant is added as signed binary digits, each by adding an unrelated register and then its complement to the upper bits.
